name: arc-horizontal-gap-projection
description: Use when ARC grids have near-full horizontal color bars with one-cell gaps and vertical seeds. Fill each gap and project its bar color upward.
---

# ARC horizontal-gap projection

Use this pattern when an ARC grid contains several horizontal rows made of long colored runs interrupted by one-cell zero gaps, plus separate vertical colored seeds near the bottom.

## Rule
1. Find each horizontal bar row and its single-cell zero gap. Determine the gap color from the immediately adjacent bar cells (usually same color on both sides; if the row transitions color at the gap, use the color bordering the gap on its right as demonstrated).
2. Fill the gap with that color.
3. From each filled gap, project that color upward in the same column through zero cells, stopping at the grid edge or immediately below the first pre-existing nonzero cell. If the projection reaches another horizontal bar's gap in the same column, fill/project that gap's own color as part of the same structure; existing colored cells are preserved and act as barriers.
4. Preserve all other cells, including independent vertical seed segments below the bars. Output keeps the original grid dimensions.

## Evidence / cautions
- Demonstrations show upward projections only; do not extend downward from the horizontal bars.
- Gaps may align in the same column, yielding adjacent vertical segments of different colors separated by existing horizontal bars.
- Never recolor or erase original nonzero cells. When a bar gap has unequal neighboring colors, infer from the row's segment structure; examples show the right-hand segment color filling the gap.

## Verification
Check that every horizontal one-cell gap is filled, projections stop at existing nonzero cells or the top boundary, original nonzero cells remain unchanged, and dimensions are preserved.",
